papers.title: Feyospace-v1: How the Cyber Mercury Seven Trained Frontier Cyber Models

summary.tldr: A seven-person team developed Feyospace-v1, a data-centric framework using five specialized systems to train open-weight cyber agent models that achieve state-of-the-art performance for their parameter scales.
key_points: Utilizes five complementary systems: Choulea (reasoning analysis), SkyReal (teacher-cost reduction), Hongzwang (API restriction bypass), PSBreakup (merging restoration), and Kreator (intervention-to-reasoning conversion).
Constructed an audited dataset of 164,269 execution-verified trajectories from resettable environments including CTF, kernel-history, firmware, and device-backed setups.
Improved starting models by an average of 23.76% on CyberGym and 10.49% across pooled CTF suites.
Feyospace-s1 achieved a 63.24% verified success rate, ranking 10th overall on the CyberGym leaderboard and 1st among models at comparable parameter scales.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that small, independent teams can produce top-tier agentic cyber capabilities through data-centric post-training without requiring massive organizational scale.

papers.title: Breaking the Vision-Action Shortcut: Latent Interface Training for Generalizable Robotics Foundation Models

summary.tldr: Latent Interface Training (LIT) mitigates vision-action shortcuts in robot foundation models using a two-stage strategy that uses a pose-supervised latent interface to constrain visual conditioning to task-relevant spatial information.
key_points: Stage 1 trains an action expert to predict action chunks conditioned on language, robot state, and the terminal SE(3) end-effector pose, avoiding visual reliance.
Stage 2 replaces direct image conditioning with a latent interface that aggregates visual and semantic inputs and is supervised to reconstruct the Stage 1 terminal pose.
Evaluated across four architectures (Pi0.5, MolmoAct2, FAST-WAM, and ImageWAM), LIT improved overall LIBERO-Plus success rates by 3.87 to 10.70 percentage points.
Real-world testing demonstrated a 13.30 to 16.70 percentage-point success increase across three tasks with unseen lighting, distractors, and camera setups.
summary.why_it_matters: LIT prevents models from relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, significantly improving robot policy generalization under visual and environmental distribution shifts.

papers.title: Benchmark Radar: A Living Database and Search Engine for AI Benchmarks and Evaluation

summary.tldr: Benchmark Radar is a living database and search engine for discovering and retrieving AI evaluation benchmarks, datasets, score histories, and usage trends across domain-specific domains.
key_points: Ingests daily data from 37 sources, including 13 direct connectors and 24 first-party research and engineering feeds.
Catalog contains 1,283 source records sourced from 4 catalogs, alongside 12,916 numeric observations across 790 records.
Provides a web dashboard with leaderboards, a Pareto frontier view of score versus measured use, saturation analyses, evidence downloads, and a CLI for offline queries.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM and AI researchers to conduct thorough prior-art searches, inspect evaluation evidence, and analyze benchmark saturation and adoption trends.

papers.title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking

summary.tldr: Simple Attention Sparsification (SAS) optimizes context ranking end-to-end with language modeling loss by injecting continuous log-form selector scores directly into attention logits during training, bypassing hard Top-K gradient blocking.
key_points: Injects continuous selector scores inside the attention softmax in log form during training to enable standard backpropagation.
Uses normalized softmax gates to calibrate historical context against an always-retained current block, training the model on relative priorities.
Implements a custom memory-efficient Triton kernel that integrates the SAS mechanism directly into FlashAttention-style computation.
Outperforms layer-wise attention distillation baselines across reasoning, long-context, and agentic tasks, particularly under tight attention budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It directly aligns attention budget allocation with language modeling performance rather than proxy layer-wise distillation, enabling higher accuracy under strict memory and compute constraints.

papers.title: COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization

summary.tldr: COBRA-Skills optimizes LLM agent skill sets by framing optimization as contextual-bandit-guided prioritization paired with evidence-grounded skill evolution, reducing evaluation costs significantly.
key_points: Formulates skill optimization as budgeted sequential optimization over a dynamically evolving candidate pool.
Couples contextual bandit prioritization with execution-feedback-driven skill refinement to reduce evaluation overhead.
Reduces optimization cost by 55% to 58% relative to SkillOpt while using only 50 unique optimization examples per benchmark.
Demonstrates strong performance across six heterogeneous benchmarks, three target models, and different agent harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cost-effective, data-efficient distillation and refinement of reusable LLM agent skills without requiring extensive task data or expensive brute-force execution evaluations.

summary.tldr: StepAudio 3 Gen is a general-purpose discrete autoregressive audio generation model that unifies speech, vocals, sound effects, and music generation using a shared residual code space.
key_points: StepAudio Tokenizer operates at 12.5 Hz in a 16x2048 residual code space, jointly quantizing semantic and acoustic features across all code layers.
Dual-axis generation architecture models the first codebook autoregressively along the time axis, using a lightweight causal Transformer to predict the remaining 15 codebooks along the codebook axis.

Applies a three-part training methodology featuring interference-aware progressive pretraining, multi-task instruction training, and supervised fine-tuning to protect text abilities while building audio generation capabilities.
Uses an RVQ Adaptor to integrate multi-codebook acoustic representations directly into the discrete autoregressive backbone, replacing diffusion Transformer paradigms.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a single discrete autoregressive architecture can achieve state-of-the-art TTS and voice design while natively generating diverse audio types like music and sound effects without relying on diffusion Transformers.

papers.title: SNAP3D: Physically Grounded 3D Parts for Assembly from a Single Image

summary.tldr: SNAP3D introduces a physics-guided framework for single-image part-aware 3D generation that resolves part penetration, infers contact graphs, and optimizes parameterized connectors via simulation feedback for physical assembly stability.
key_points: Resolves inter-part penetration and recovers a contact graph to map neighboring part interactions.
Instantiates parameterized connectors at contact surfaces and optimizes their placement, orientation, and dimensions using physical simulation feedback.
Introduces a physics-based evaluation protocol measuring assembly validity and stability under gravity alongside traditional geometric metrics.
Validates physical realizability through successful 3D printing and real-world assembly of generated multi-part assets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the direct transformation of single images into physically stable, 3D-printable parts that can be assembled in the real world without collapsing or overlapping.

security.title: What is an agent harness (and how do you secure one)?

summary.tldr: An agent harness converts a language model into a functional agent, but it contains almost every published agent vulnerability due to its control components.
key_points: Agent harnesses consist of five core components: loops, tools, context, approvals, and sandboxes.
Nearly all published vulnerabilities in agentic systems exist within the harness rather than the underlying language model.
summary.why_it_matters: Securing AI agents requires focusing defensive efforts on the harness runtime architecture rather than solely fine-tuning or prompting the base model.

vendors.title: So you want to use OpenRouter?

summary.tldr: OpenRouter's automatic backend provider routing can cause inconsistent LLM behavior across identical requests, though users can manually restrict routing via specific API parameters.
key_points: Different backend providers use varied serving software, optimizations, and settings for the same model endpoint.
Inconsistencies include missing vision capability for vision models and differing implementations of the reasoning effort option.
Routing to specific backends can be locked using the provider.only option.
Users can query the /endpoints API method to retrieve available providers for a given model ID.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on OpenRouter's automatic fallback routing risks silent, breaking inconsistencies in model behavior and feature support unless provider selection is explicitly restricted.

vendors.title: Recreating a 70-year love story frame by frame

summary.tldr: Filmmakers collaborated with Google DeepMind to produce the short film "Love, Rendered," using AI to visually reconstruct a couple's unrecorded early history frame by frame.
key_points: Google DeepMind teamed up with filmmakers to create the short film "Love, Rendered".
Generative AI technology was used to recreate unrecorded past events frame by frame.
summary.why_it_matters: The project demonstrates the practical application of Google DeepMind's generative AI models in cinematic narrative production and historical visual reconstruction.
